Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to StellarTech’s Q2 2024 earnings call. With me today are Robert Miller, CEO; Susan Chen, CFO; Michael Evans, COO; and David Lee, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Robert.

Robert Miller, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet, and welcome, everyone.

We had a strong quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to address our sales guidance, forecast, and trend analysis by segment for the next quarter and the full year. While the overall global smartphone market faces headwinds in 2020, our diversification strategy and targeted investments in 5G technology position us to outperform the market average. We anticipate a stronger second half of the year driven by the launch of new 5G devices and strategic partnerships in key growth regions. Our semiconductor business, excluding memory, is expected to hold steady, benefiting from increased demand in specific sectors despite the overall economic slowdown. The foundry segment, a key growth area, is projected to deliver substantial revenue gains, further validating our investments in advanced process technologies. For the smartphone segment, we are projecting that our 5G-related revenues will grow by over 60% year-over-year in Q3 2020, contributing approximately 35% of our total smartphone component sales. We are guiding for a 5-7% sequential increase in smartphone component revenue in Q3 2020 compared to Q2 2020, driven by the ramp-up of new 5G smartphone models from our key partners. This translates to approximately $1.85 - $1.90 billion in revenue for the segment in Q3. We expect our semiconductor business (excluding memory) to be relatively stable in 2020, with revenue declining by approximately 2-4% year-over-year, slightly better than the overall market forecast. We are guiding for a slight increase (1-3%) in semiconductor revenue (excluding memory) in Q3 2020 compared to Q2 2020, driven by strong demand in the data center and industrial sectors. We are very optimistic about the growth prospects of our foundry business, projecting revenue growth of 18-20% for the full year 2020, significantly outperforming the overall semiconductor market. We are guiding for a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by the ramp-up of 7nm production and increased demand for our specialty technologies. Considering the performance of each segment, we are reaffirming our full-year 2020 revenue guidance of approximately $18 billion. We expect a stronger second half of the year, driven by the recovery in the smartphone market, the continued strength of our data center business, and the rapid growth of our foundry segment.

We also made meaningful progress with our gross margin results. Our Q2 2024 gross margin reached 53%, a 1.2 percentage point improvement compared to Q1 2024's 51.8%. This positive trend is primarily attributable to a confluence of factors, most notably sustained high capacity utilization and the absence of inventory valuation adjustments that negatively impacted us in the previous quarter. We saw an average capacity utilization rate of 96% across our major fabrication facilities in Q2, compared to 92% in Q1. The absence of the unfavorable inventory valuation adjustment of $45 million related to legacy product lines that we recorded in Q1 provided a positive tailwind, contributing approximately 0.5 percentage points to the gross margin. The appreciation of the New Taiwan Dollar (NT$) against the US Dollar in Q2 presented a headwind, decreasing gross margin by approximately 0.3 percentage points. For Q3 2024, we are guiding for a gross margin between 50% and 52%. The midpoint of this range, 51%, is higher than our previous guidance of 49-51% provided three months ago during the Q1 earnings call. Looking ahead to Q4 2024, we anticipate a dilution of our gross margin by approximately 2 to 3 percentage points due to the continued steep ramp-up of our 5nm technology. The 5nm process node represents our most advanced technology offering, and its ramp-up requires significant investment in new equipment, process optimization, and yield enhancement.

On a broader level, our utilization rate has supported our positioning. Our Q3 gross margin midpoint significantly exceeded our initial guidance provided three months ago. A key contributor to this positive surprise was a consistently high level of overall capacity utilization across our global manufacturing facilities, despite the ongoing uncertainties related to COVID-19 and its regional impacts. In Q3, our overall capacity utilization rate averaged 92.5%, a substantial increase compared to 87.8% in Q2 and 84.1% in Q3 of last year. Looking ahead to Q4, we anticipate a slight moderation in utilization rates, projecting an average of 90-91%. We are investing heavily in expanding our capacity to meet the growing demand for our products, and are on track to bring our new facility in Arizona online in the first half of next year, which will add approximately 10% to our overall production capacity.

I’ll now hand it over to Susan to walk you through the financials.

Susan Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, the increased capital expenditure helped drive improvements in our manufacturing capabilities. TSMC's CapEx for Q2 2020 totaled NT$127 billion, which translates to approximately US$4.2 billion. This figure represents a slight decrease of approximately 3% compared to Q1 2020. A significant portion of the US$4.2 billion was allocated to accelerating the ramp-up of our 5nm process technology, approximately 60% or $2.52 billion. We estimate 25%, or $1.05 billion, was directed towards 7nm enhancement and capacity maintenance. Roughly 10% or $420 million went into advanced packaging technologies.

Additionally, our wafer sales showed strong performance. Overall, Q2 saw a healthy 12% increase in wafer revenue year-over-year to $2.15 billion, driven primarily by increased demand for advanced technology nodes, particularly in the high-performance computing (HPC) and automotive sectors. The 7nm node contributed 36% of total wafer revenue, translating to approximately $774 million. We shipped approximately 1.2 million wafers at the 7nm node, with an average selling price (ASP) of $645 per wafer. The 16nm node maintained a robust contribution, accounting for 18% of total wafer revenue, or approximately $387 million. We shipped around 1.8 million wafers at the 16nm node, with an ASP of $215 per wafer. In total, we shipped approximately 5.5 million wafers in Q2 2024. The overall weighted average selling price (ASP) across all technology nodes was approximately $391 per wafer.

Our operating margin results also showed improvement, where we’ve increased efficiencies and controlled costs. Our operating margin performance in Q2 2024 demonstrated strong execution and exceeded initial expectations, landing at 42.2%. This represents a significant 0.8 percentage point improvement sequentially compared to Q1 2024's operating margin of 41.4%. Looking at the year-over-year (YoY) comparison, the operating margin increased by a substantial 2.1 percentage points from Q2 2023's 40.1%. The 0.8 percentage point sequential increase in operating margin can be attributed to revenue growth outpacing cost of goods sold (COGS) increase, improved operational efficiency, strategic pricing adjustments, and favorable currency exchange rates. The significant 2.1 percentage point YoY increase in operating margin is a testament to the effectiveness of our long-term strategic initiatives, the successful integration of the Acme Corp acquisition, the shift to higher-margin revenue streams, operating expense leverage, and reduced research and development (R&D) spending as a percentage of revenue. During our Q1 2024 earnings call, we provided operating margin guidance of between 39% and 41% for Q2 2024. Our actual operating margin of 42.2% significantly exceeded this guidance, primarily due to the underestimated impact of Project Phoenix, conservative cost projections, and faster realization of synergies from Acme Corp. For Q3 2024, we are providing operating margin guidance of between 39% and 41%.

Now I’ll pass it to Michael to provide color on execution.

Michael Evans, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was our sales guidance, as Robert mentioned earlier. Despite the market downturn, we anticipate a more resilient performance in our smartphone component sales, projecting a decline of approximately 8-10% year-over-year for the full year 2020. We have solidified strategic partnerships with key smartphone OEMs, particularly in China and South Korea, who are aggressively pushing 5G adoption. These partnerships secure a significant portion of our 5G component demand. Our strong presence in the Asia-Pacific region (excluding Japan) helps offset some of the weakness in North America and Europe. We are particularly optimistic about growth in India, where smartphone penetration is still relatively low and 5G infrastructure development is accelerating.

We also saw execution gains related to our wafer sales. We anticipate continued strong growth in wafer sales in Q3 2024, projecting a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. This growth will be driven by further ramp-up of 7nm+ production, particularly for HPC applications, increased demand for 16nm wafers from the automotive sector, and continued progress in our 5nm node development, with initial pilot production expected to commence in late Q3. We are actively managing our legacy node capacity, prioritizing applications with higher margins and phasing out production of commodity chips where possible.

Lastly, we began pilots tied to our CapEx guidance for the full year. Based on the strong demand environment and our strategic commitment to maintaining technology leadership, StellarTech has increased its full-year 2020 CapEx guidance to a range of US$16 billion to US$17 billion, a notable increase from the previous guidance of US$15 billion to US$16 billion issued three months ago. The primary driver of this increase is the accelerated investment in advanced technologies, specifically 5nm demand surge and 3nm readiness. We are allocating a significant portion of the incremental CapEx to expand our 5nm capacity. Capital intensity for 2020 is expected to be slightly lower than 40%, and we anticipate our capital intensity will gradually decline to above the mid-30s over the long term. The majority of our CapEx investments are concentrated in Taiwan.

Now I’ll turn it over to David to discuss our new fab construction progress.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Michael.

On the technology side, our teams delivered important milestones across multiple streams.

First, we completed major feature work aligned with our gross margin targets, especially regarding capacity utilization and cost management. Our Q2 2024 gross margin reached 53%, a 1.2 percentage point improvement compared to Q1 2024's 51.8%. This positive trend is primarily attributable to sustained high capacity utilization and the absence of inventory valuation adjustments that negatively impacted us in the previous quarter. High capacity utilization allowed us to absorb fixed manufacturing costs more efficiently, directly contributing to the gross margin expansion. The absence of the unfavorable inventory valuation adjustment of $45 million related to legacy product lines that we recorded in Q1 provided a positive tailwind, contributing approximately 0.5 percentage points to the gross margin.

We also rolled out enhancements supporting our operating margin improvements. Our operating margin performance in Q2 2024 demonstrated strong execution and exceeded initial expectations, landing at 42.2%. This represents a significant 0.8 percentage point improvement sequentially compared to Q1 2024's operating margin of 41.4%. The 0.8 percentage point sequential increase in operating margin can be attributed to revenue growth outpacing cost of goods sold (COGS) increase, improved operational efficiency, strategic pricing adjustments, and favorable currency exchange rates.

One final point — we’ve made structural improvements to better enable our new fab construction progress. This quarter marks a period of significant, albeit measured, progress in the construction of StellarTech's Arizona-based advanced semiconductor fabrication facility. We are pleased to report the completion of the core building shell for Phase 1 of the fab. Critical utility infrastructure, including the high-purity water system, industrial gas supply (nitrogen, argon, oxygen), and advanced power distribution network, are progressing according to plan. A dedicated logistics hub is now fully operational on-site. While full-scale tool move-in is slated for Q4 2023 and Q1 2024, we've seen the arrival and initial installation of several key pieces of equipment, primarily focused on metrology and quality control. StellarTech's close collaboration with key equipment suppliers, including ASML, Applied Materials, and Lam Research, remains crucial. StellarTech has initiated comprehensive training programs for its U.S.-based workforce, focusing on the operation and maintenance of advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The Arizona fab project continues to represent a substantial capital expenditure for StellarTech, with the total investment for Phase 1 estimated at $12 billion.

Let’s now open the floor for Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. You mentioned gains in utilization rate. What gives you confidence that these are sustainable?

Robert Miller:
We are seeing some opportunities to increase prices in certain segments where demand is particularly strong and our products offer a clear value proposition. However, we are also mindful of the need to maintain our competitiveness and build long-term relationships with our customers. We are carefully balancing price increases with cost reductions and efficiency improvements to maximize our profitability without compromising our market position.

Analyst 2:
On capital expenditure, is this going to impact our debt levels?

Susan Chen:
We are certainly seeing some tightness in the labor market, particularly for skilled technicians and engineers. We are addressing this challenge through a combination of strategies, including increased investment in training and development, competitive compensation packages, and partnerships with local universities and technical colleges. We are also exploring automation solutions to reduce our reliance on manual labor in certain areas of our operations.

Analyst 3:
Can you elaborate on early traction with your CapEx guidance?

Michael Evans:
While we acknowledge the ongoing uncertainties, our current backlog and customer forecasts give us confidence in our ability to maintain strong utilization rates in 2024. The diversity of our customer base and the breadth of our product portfolio also provide us with a degree of resilience in the face of macroeconomic headwinds. Our investments in automation and process optimization will further enhance our ability to respond to changing market conditions and maintain high utilization rates.

Analyst 4:
How are you thinking about long-term opportunity in the fab construction in Arizona?

David Lee:
The Arizona fab is strategically positioned to address the growing demand for high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and advanced mobile applications. We project that the Arizona fab will contribute approximately 8% to TSMC's overall revenue in 2025, based on the planned 20,000 wafers per month capacity.

Closing

Robert Miller:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us. We’re energized by the results this quarter and remain focused on disciplined execution and strategic expansion. Looking forward to sharing continued progress next time.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
